scope_rule: Includes immutable value objects and accepted artifacts used by more than one jurisdiction or material family. Jurisdiction-specific legal semantics, runtime components, stores, and derived views remain with their existing owners and are not generalized here.

objects.fingerprint_basis: Referenced object identity plus its exact declared fingerprint
invariants: Reference type is closed
Identity and fingerprint are both required
Mutable aliases and locators cannot substitute for the reference

objects.fingerprint_basis: Exact immutable contract bytes
invariants: Contract ID, semantic version, and fingerprint are all required
Floating versions are forbidden

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over exact declared file bytes
invariants: Path is relative and contained
Role, media type, byte size, and fingerprint are exact
One path occurs once per inventory

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over the complete immutable input set
invariants: One idempotency key cannot bind different input fingerprints
Exact replay returns the recorded result without repeating effects

objects.fingerprint_basis: Contained by the fingerprinted decision or report
invariants: Every applied rule names the exact rulebook and immutable decision
Trace order is preserved by the containing artifact

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS object bytes, stored externally
invariants: Source authority and intended use are explicit
UNDECIDED and DISABLED are represented without a default
Credentials are absent

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS object bytes, stored externally
invariants: Endpoint is separate from source authority
Connector contract is exact
Credential values are absent

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS object bytes, stored externally
invariants: Source failure is not no change
Cutoff and observation time are explicit UTC timestamps
Replay is fingerprint-bound
External effects are NONE

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over exact captured artifact bytes and the canonical snapshot object
invariants: At least one exact captured artifact is inventoried
Artifact paths are contained and hash-bound
Snapshot bytes are never mutated

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS object bytes, stored externally
invariants: Unknown source meaning is not guessed
Resolution is a new immutable reference
Review policy remains separately configured

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over the canonical root manifest binding every exact component
invariants: One package owns one jurisdiction-and-material pair
Every scope has explicit readiness
Unresolved policy is visible
A new version never rewrites an old decision

objects.fingerprint_basis: Contained by the Source Rulebook Package fingerprint
invariants: State is exactly DECISION_READY or NOT_READY
Not-ready blockers are explicit
Readiness of one scope does not infer another

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS attestation bytes, stored externally
invariants: Exact rulebook, build, and suites are bound
Reproducibility is explicit
Attestation creates no production effect

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS decision bytes, stored externally
invariants: Decision is cutoff-bound
Facts and unresolved facts stay separate
Rule Trace and evidence are exact
Decision does not approve production

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS registration bytes, stored externally
invariants: Identity is register-issued
Source locators and text do not determine identity
Identity is never reused or deleted

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS registration bytes and exact official evidence
invariants: One version belongs to one Legal Item
Legal status events do not invent versions
Predecessor lineage is forward and acyclic

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS event bytes, stored externally
invariants: Event and Official Version remain distinct
Effective expression and cutoff are explicit
Evidence and decision are required

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS registration bytes, stored externally
invariants: Visible numbering does not determine identity
Ended locations remain preserved
Continuity requires evidence and the material rulebook

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS alias bytes, stored externally
invariants: Alias is evidence and never authority for identity
Owner identity is exact
Historical alias remains preserved

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS relationship bytes, stored externally
invariants: One-to-one, one-to-many, and many-to-one are representable
Cycles are forbidden
Relationship is evidence-backed
Selection history is separate

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS event bytes, stored externally
invariants: Selection history does not create backward record lineage
Reselection may reuse an exact preserved record
Retirement is deselection rather than deletion

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS scope bytes, stored externally
invariants: Scope is stable and non-overlapping
One responsible Legal Desk owns it
One Search Record has exactly one scope owner per target

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS registry bytes, stored externally
invariants: All required scopes are listed exactly once
Complete non-overlap proof is exact
A new registry version never mutates an old inventory

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over canonical complete release manifest and referenced exact records
invariants: Release is complete for one scope and cutoff
It is not a delta
Record count and fingerprint match exact records
A bare empty release cannot hide a gap

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over canonical complete withholding release manifest
invariants: release_kind is WITHHOLDING
Every omitted subject or prior record is explicitly accounted
Withholding never deletes identity or evidence

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS selection bytes, stored externally
invariants: Carry-forward is explicit and never silent
Last-verified time and Coverage Gap are required
Review policy is CONFIGURED or explicitly UNDECIDED

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over canonical complete scope and flattened target views
invariants: Every required scope is selected exactly once
Scope and flattened views agree
Record IDs are target-wide unique
Counts, ordering, ownership, and fingerprints are exact

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS gap bytes, stored externally
invariants: Known gap is visible and evidence-backed
Open gap is not no relevant law
Resolution appends a new exact reference

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS quarantine bytes, stored externally
invariants: Uncertainty is preserved rather than guessed
Quarantine is not retirement
Review policy remains separately bound

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over canonical complete status manifest bytes
invariants: Every required scope has one status
Gaps, quarantines, and source failures remain distinguishable
Signature policy is explicitly UNDECIDED until settled

objects.fingerprint_basis: serving_payload_fingerprint is SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS metadata bytes; ID is excluded
invariants: Outer object contains only id and metadata
Metadata contains exactly six required strings
authority_note is always present and None is the only no-note sentinel
Any payload change selects a different exact record

objects.fingerprint_basis: One JCS-canonical NDJSON line inside an exact shard
invariants: Exactly one entry exists per desired Search Record
Ownership and serving payload fingerprint agree
Authority-note fingerprint and decision agree
Arrays are sorted and duplicate-free

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over exact canonical NDJSON bytes including final LF, or zero bytes for an empty shard
invariants: One shard exists for every selected Release Scope
Path is derived from shard ID
Entries are sorted by Search Record ID
No undeclared shard is discovered

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS root manifest bytes, which transitively bind every shard
invariants: Total count equals shard and desired-state counts
Exactly one entry exists per desired record and no orphan exists
The manifest does not fingerprint itself
Lookup is outside the live query path

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS contract bytes, stored externally
invariants: Embedding input is metadata.text only
Downstream receives text and authority_note
No runtime traceability join exists
User-facing policy remains explicitly UNDECIDED

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over canonical immutable generation definition and exact verification evidence
invariants: Generation is complete for one jurisdiction target
Desired state and configuration are exact
Name policy remains explicitly UNDECIDED
No live target is mutated in place by this object

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS complete routing generation bytes, stored externally
invariants: Every served jurisdiction has one exact target
Every request pins one complete generation
Activation mechanism remains explicitly UNDECIDED
latest aliases are not authority

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS definition bytes and every exact immutable reference
invariants: Definition is sealed before Approval
Approval and execution receipts are excluded
Definition does not refer back to Promotion Manifest
Creating the definition grants no eligibility or activation

objects.fingerprint_basis: Same immutable definition fingerprint; eligibility is proved by separate lifecycle events
invariants: Serving State is not a second mutable object
Build and verification events establish eligibility
Exactly one state is active per environment

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS event bytes, stored externally
invariants: Events append and never mutate definitions
Only activation and rollback activation change active state
Expected-base compare-and-set is required
Event identifies one serving period

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS manifest bytes and all exact bound references
invariants: Manifest is the sole execution envelope
Full corpus payloads and secrets are absent
Cost policy is UNDECIDED and execution capability is DISABLED in this foundation
Any material change requires a new manifest

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS decision bytes, stored externally
invariants: One decision binds one exact manifest identity and fingerprint
Rejection is terminal
Approval is all-or-nothing
Governance policy remains explicitly UNDECIDED

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS event bytes, stored externally
invariants: Revocation, expiry, invalidation, and consumption append
Decision is never rewritten
Consumption binds one execution lineage

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS event bytes, stored externally
invariants: Every retry stays in one lineage with exact input fingerprint
Receipts are append-only
Effects are NONE or one declared manifest action
No event broadens Approval

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS exact task contract bytes, stored externally
invariants: Task allocation is explicit and may remain UNDECIDED or DISABLED
Output is proposal only
Forbidden decisions are enumerated
Only the sole task runner may call a generative provider

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS complete workflow profile bytes and all result-affecting references
invariants: Admission covers one exact complete workflow
Provider, threshold, security, and retention policies remain UNDECIDED in this foundation
A floating model alias cannot be bound

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS event bytes, stored externally
invariants: Only ADMITTED may process declared new work
Suspension stops new calls
Revocation and supersession preserve historical results

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS exact capability profile bytes and all bound components
invariants: Capabilities are least-privilege and owner-bound
Profile grants no use before attestation and activation
Deferred policies are explicit
One capability never implies another

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS attestation bytes, stored externally
invariants: Exact profile and complete results are bound
Limitations are explicit
Attestation has no external effect
Activation remains separate

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS event bytes, stored externally
invariants: State changes append
Active scope cannot exceed the profile
Suspended or revoked capability processes no new work
Reactivation requires exact revalidation

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS status bytes, stored externally
invariants: Every operational capability has an explicit disabled state
Deferred decisions are named
Production stack is UNDECIDED
External effects are NONE

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS manifest bytes, stored externally; manifest does not inventory itself
invariants: Every package file except the root manifest is listed exactly once
Paths are contained
Byte sizes and hashes are exact
Undeclared files fail

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS catalogue bytes
invariants: Codes are unique and sorted
Unknown codes fail
Meaning changes require a new version
Catalogue presence grants no capability or legal outcome

objects.fingerprint_basis: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS state-machine bytes
invariants: Allowed transitions are exact
Every unlisted transition is forbidden
High-risk forbidden transitions are named
All states are closed lifecycle codes and reachable

excluded_categories.reason: These accepted artifacts contain jurisdiction- or material-specific legal semantics and remain governed by their exact Source Rulebooks and ADRs. Generalizing them would silently choose legal policy.

These are applications, components, or durable interfaces rather than immutable cross-cutting domain artifacts. This foundation defines the objects they exchange without selecting their implementation stack.
These are fields, calculated values, or projections whose source object is already inventoried. Duplicating them as mutable standalone records would create competing authority.
